articles.title: 11-year-old boy 'molested' at Satlok Ashram in Haryana; sevadar arrested
articles.summary: SONIPAT: An 11-year-old boy was allegedly molested at Satlok Ashram in Dhanana village, Sonipat, prompting the Baroda police to register a case and arrest
articles.body: SONIPAT: An 11-year-old boy was allegedly molested at Satlok Ashram in Dhanana village, Sonipat, prompting the Baroda police to register a case and arrest a man identified as Sachin, a resident of Kansadi village in Sonipat district.According to the Sonipat Police, the accused was arrested on September 24 and subsequently produced before a court, which sent him to judicial custody.The police action followed information received from the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) regarding the alleged incident involving the minor at Satlok Ashram in Dhanana village, Sonipat.According to the police, the CWC chairperson informed Baroda police on September 23 that an 11-year-old boy who had come to Satlok Ashram in Dhanana village, Sonipat, had allegedly been subjected to inappropriate physical contact with sexual intent.A police team reached the location and took the minor into protective care along with his father. The child was subsequently taken to a concerned institution/hospital in Khanpur Kalan for legal assistance, counselling and medical procedures.Police said that during counselling, the child provided information about the alleged incident.Based on the statement given by the child's father and the information received from the CWC, police registered an FIR at Baroda police station on September 24 under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.The accused, identified as Sachin of Kansadi village, was arrested the same day. Police said he was questioned and further legal proceedings were initiated.He was later produced before a court and sent to judicial custody.DCP says accused was a sevadar at Dhanana AshramDCP (HPS) Gohana Jitendra Gehlawat, while briefing journalists, said Sachin was serving as a sevadar at Satlok Ashram in Dhanana village, Sonipat, and had taken naam diksha from Sant Rampal Maharaj.The police statement, therefore, describes the accused as being associated with the ashram.The Satlok Ashram committee has presented a different account.Committee member Om Prakash Saini said the matter was known to the committee but claimed that the boy from Kansadi village had no connection with the ashram. He also said that the boy had not taken initiation from Sant Rampal Maharaj.According to Saini, a dispute had taken place between the two boys on a bus and nothing happened inside Satlok Ashram in Dhanana village, Sonipat. He claimed that whatever happened occurred outside the ashram premises.Saini also said that the ashram management itself called the police after learning about the matter and that the committee was monitoring the case while the police conducted their investigation.Satlok Ashram spokesperson Rahul also said that, to his knowledge, no such incident had taken place and that misleading information was being circulated. articles.title: Over 100 students walk 40km to Buxar, protest school conditions
articles.summary: Over 100 Ambedkar Residential School students marched 40km to Buxar, protesting lack of water, power and food quality; officials promised action.
articles.body: Buxar: More than 100 students of Ambedkar Residential School at Rampur village in Kesath block of Dumraon subdivision walked nearly 40km to Buxar on Sunday and staged a protest at Ambedkar Chowk, alleging poor living conditions and lack of basic facilities.Students from classes III to X began the march early in the morning and reached the district headquarters in the afternoon. Wearing soiled clothes, visibly tired and with several younger children walking barefoot, they sat on the road and raised slogans over their grievances.The students alleged the school had been without regular water and electricity for several days. They claimed they were forced to use water from a nearby canal and also complained about the quality of food, alleging insects had been found in meals on some occasions.Student Vishal Kumar said repeated complaints to teachers and officials had gone unaddressed. He alleged food, drinking water, electricity, uniforms and other essential facilities were inadequate.The protesters demanded restoration of basic facilities, better meals and action against those responsible. They also sought removal of district welfare officer (DWO) Arvind Kumar, alleging their complaints had not been addressed.Buxar SDM Avinash Kumar and SDPO Gaurav Pandey reached the spot and tried to persuade the students to end the road blockade. The protesters insisted on meeting district magistrate Sahila and submitting their grievances. AISA supporters and other social organisations also joined them.The DWO rejected the allegations, saying the school had a generator and drinking water was arranged through it during power cuts. He also denied complaints about food quality.“Power supply was disrupted for three days, but drinking water was arranged through the generator. Food is served strictly according to the prescribed menu. I personally visited the school on Saturday and mutton and rice were served as per the menu,” Kumar said, adding the allegations were baseless.The protest ended around 6pm after ADM Arun Kumar met with the students and pacified them. The SDM and other officials assured the students that their complaints would be heard and a written representation accepted.
